chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskān said: Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār narrated to me from ʿUmar ibn Yazīd who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) about the ṭāʾmith (woman who begins menstruation before entering the state of iḥrām for Hajj), and he said: 'She fulfills all the rituals, except that she does not perform tawāf between aṣ-Ṣafā and al-Marwah.'

I said: 'For some of what she fulfills from the rituals is greater than aṣ-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, namely al-mawqif (standing at ʿArafāt). So why is it that she fulfills the rituals but does not perform tawāf between aṣ-Ṣafā and al-Marwah?'
He said: 'Because aṣ-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, she performs tawāf with them whenever she wishes, and indeed these al-mawāqif (standing places) she cannot fulfill them if they pass her by.'

key_terms.اَلصَّفَا: Al-Ṣafā, one of the two hills between which tawāf is performed
key_terms.اَلطَّامِث: A woman who begins menstruating before entering the state of iḥrām for Hajj
key_terms.اَلْمَرْوَةِ: Al-Marwah, the second of the two hills between which tawāf is performed
key_terms.اَلْمَوْقِف: The standing (at ʿArafāt), a core pillar of Hajj

ai.seo_question: What rituals does a woman miss if she starts menstruating before entering iḥrām for Hajj?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the distinction between time-bound obligations (*waqt*) and non-time-bound acts in Hajj jurisprudence. He explains that while standing at the mawāqif is lost if missed due to menstruation, the Sa'i between al-Safa and al-Marwah can be performed later at the pilgrim's convenience, highlighting the flexibility of ritual compensation (*qada*) in Shia fiqh.
